sourceDigestNormalization: UTF-8 source bytes with CRLF normalized to LF
coverage: PostgreSQL restore CLI supports explicit --resume using the same backup/manifest/ledger/target binding and shared atomic file-copy protocol as SQLite.
Database guard and import runtime initialize in one transaction; an interrupted pre-initialization resumes only into a genuinely empty target database.

Independent operation transaction, controller session lock, native import transaction lock and reserved epoch protect distinct phases. Prepared/imported/completed states decide whether to import, reapply rolled-back cleanup or finish the receipt only.

Pre-cleanup core-table fingerprint, schema summary and referenced files are checked against the verified backup before applying a deletion ledger. Physical source/media cleanup can replenish missing bytes and revalidate ownership after a rolled-back interruption.

Final receipt and actual retained/deleted file states commit with ready in the runtime schema excluded from future backups. The returned/printed JSONB representation is the same canonical result used by later receipt publication.

Nineteen new real PostgreSQL cases cover fourteen actual parent SIGKILL phases, a competing live controller, legal new learning followed by idempotent receipt retrieval, changed backup/ledger/database/imported data, media cleanup failure and actual native CLI resume.

Existing twenty-case PostgreSQL native import/cold restore run remains passing after integration, including independent live native locking, delayed epoch rejection, tool errors, backup exclusion and copy-time junction refusal.
